newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuanian PM says to find more funds for budget.
newsitem.headline: Lithuanian PM says to find more funds for budget.

text.p: New Lithuanian Prime Minister Gediminas Vagnorius said on Thursday that the government hoped to find some 305 million litas more revenue for the 1997 budget, which is planned with a deficit of 697 million litas.
Vagnorius was presenting a new budget draft for a second reading, which amends the budget planned by the old government. The new budget deficit is some 100 million litas larger.

"The budget is to be amended to meet the government programme, especially for the first half of 1997, and to improve the economic, social and financial situation of the country," Vagnorius told a news conference.

The new cabinet intends to collect an additional 305 million litas by implementing various economic measures, such as better tax administration and tougher smuggling controls. Some 450 million litas are to come from cutting other expenses.

The government has also decided on a tax reform to be implemented from the second quarter of 1997 with profits invested in job creation to be exempted from taxation. Income tax is to be reformed from July 1, 1997, he added.

The government also decided to allocate 45 million litas to boost exports and another 40 million litas are be used for the creation of jobs in small and medium size businesses, he added. Additional state funds are also planned for house building.
